name: Scenario 4: RAG Retrieval & Usage
query: How much protein should I consume per day for muscle gains?

matchedCards.claim: For resistance-trained, lean athletes undergoing a caloric restriction to lose fat, dietary protein needs are elevated to 2.3-3.1 g/kg of fat-free mass to prevent muscle loss.
practicalAdvice: When eating in a calorie deficit, prioritize high protein intake to signal your body to retain muscle mass while losing fat.
The leaner you are and the larger the deficit, the more protein you need to protect your muscle tissue.

source.title: A systematic review of dietary protein during caloric restriction in resistance trained lean athletes: a case for higher intakes
source.organization: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
source.scope: Resistance trained lean athletes; protein needs during caloric restriction.

dosage.note: 2.3 to 3.1 g/kg of fat-free mass (FFM) is generally higher than standard protein recommendations.

matchedCards.claim: In healthy adults performing prolonged resistance training, protein supplementation can modestly improve gains in muscle size and strength.
practicalAdvice: Emphasize that resistance training remains the main stimulus.
Treat protein supplements as a convenient option, not a requirement.
Encourage food-based protein sources when practical.

source.title: A Systematic Review, Meta-analysis and Meta-regression of the Effect of Protein Supplementation on Resistance Training-induced Gains in Muscle Mass and Strength in Healthy Adults
source.scope: Healthy adults performing resistance exercise training for at least 6 weeks; protein supplementation and training adaptations.

excludedPopulation: children and adolescents unless reviewed separately
limitations: The review studied healthy adults and supplementation during resistance training lasting at least 6 weeks.
